catalog.summary: One region whose content shows or hides.

labelPart.reason: The words get a box of their own, as they do in `tabs` and `tag`: it is what `text-overflow` needs to clip a title the row cannot grow for, what `unicode-bidi: isolate` needs to keep a title in another script from reordering the row around it, and what the indicator's column is aligned against. `isolate` rather than the `plaintext` those two use, because a heading takes its alignment from the page: the first right-to-left capture showed a Latin title stranded against the far edge of an Arabic page.

wiring.aria-expanded: true on the trigger while the panel is open, false while it is closed
wiring.aria-level: the heading element itself in React, which renders h1 to h6 from `level`; in Angular the consumer writes the element and the directive supplies role="heading" and aria-level only when what they wrote is not a heading, which the pattern names as the alternative to a native one
wiring.aria-disabled: true on a trigger the group refuses to let close
wiring.aria-busy: true on the panel while the family is loading
wiring.panelRole: region only when the consumer asks for it, because a region is a landmark

heading.reason: The APG requires the header button to be wrapped in an element with role heading and an appropriate aria-level, and requires that button to be the only element inside it. `actions` is therefore a sibling of the header rather than a child, and a standalone disclosure that is not part of an outline uses `none`, which writes no heading semantics at all. React renders the element from `level`; Angular takes the element the consumer wrote — the directive on their own element is what that ecosystem composes with — and supplies the role and the level when it is not already a heading. Both reach the same accessibility tree, and the pattern names both as acceptable.

keyboard.effect: moves to the next focusable element; the trigger, everything in the actions slot and everything inside an open panel are all in the page tab sequence
moves to the previous focusable element, under the same rule

detailsElement.reason: `details` and `summary` supply the disclosure role, Enter, Space, find-in-page and — through `name` — exclusive opening, and the family still refuses them. The accordion pattern requires the trigger to be the only element inside a heading, and `summary` may neither be wrapped in one nor hold one without putting the heading inside the button; `details` opens itself, so a controlled family is a frame behind and has to write the value back; `name` expresses exclusive opening and neither `multiple` nor `requireOpen` nor a cancellable request carrying a reason; and animating `::details-content` to an intrinsic height still needs `interpolate-size`, which MDN records as limited availability. The cost is written on the reference page: a page with JavaScript disabled cannot open a panel, and find-in-page reaches closed content only through mount="until-found".

horizontalCollapse.reason: Radix and Base UI both expose a content width for a panel that opens sideways, and neither ships a use for it. A drawer that opens along the inline axis is `sidebar`'s, and a consumer needing it today overrides `grid-template-rows` with `grid-template-columns` on the panel in three lines.

focusOnOpen.reason: No surveyed implementation moves focus into a panel it opened, and the APG does not ask for it. The trigger keeps focus, so a reader who opened three panels in a row is still where they were; a consumer whose panel holds a form focuses its own first field.

mount.active: the panel's content exists only while it is open; the box stays, so the trigger's aria-controls never names an element that is gone
mount.lazy: the content is built on the first open and kept afterwards
mount.eager: the content exists from the start, which is what lets the panel transition closed
mount.until-found: the panel exists from the start and carries hidden="until-found" while closed, so the browser's own find-in-page opens it
mount.reason: One axis with four values rather than the three booleans the field ships — forceMount, keepMounted, lazyMount, unmountOnExit, hiddenUntilFound — which admit combinations that mean nothing. The default is eager because content that is not in the DOM has nothing to transition; `active` is the answer for a panel holding a table, and its cost is that closing is instant. What is dropped is the content and never the box: Radix and Base UI remove the whole panel, and the trigger's aria-controls then names an element that is not there.

motion.reason: Radix writes --radix-collapsible-content-height, Base UI --collapsible-panel-height, and Ark and Angular Material each measure in their own words. A measured height is wrong for one frame in a server response and stale until a resize observer fires. A grid track transitioning between 0fr and 1fr is the content's own height at every frame, and nothing reads the layout.

findInPage.reason: The vocabulary in docs/state-and-events.md holds no reason for a browser's page search. The move is the browser's rather than an interaction with this family's own control, so it carries `programmatic`; adding a twelfth reason is a change to a contract outside this family.
